S065-01.notes: 'had only recently become affordable in Japan: ... once too costly ... cheap enough' reads cleanly; the colon clause defines the blank. A obsolete contradicts recent heavy use; C illegal has no support (the issue was cost, not law); D decorative ignores the cost contrast. Facts (Prussian blue imported via Dutch/Chinese trade, cheap by late 1820s, Great Wave c. 1831) are accurate.

S065-02.notes: The skin stripes led to the forest-zebra guess, but the skulls matched giraffes, so the stripes misled scientists. A: nothing is said about what local people believed; the zebra guess came from scientists. B: no claim about giraffe ancestors having stripes. D reverses the lesson, since the skulls corrected the skin-based guess.

S065-03.notes: The claim is about B's advantage over A changing with light, so the answer needs the B-minus-A gap at both light levels: 8 cm vs 1 cm. B gives one value and no comparison across light levels. C gives only fertilizer A's light effect. D shows that light helps both fertilizers but says nothing about the gap between them.

S065-04.notes: Text 2 shows Wallace reached the idea independently and the two men's papers were presented together, so the 'Darwin alone' accounts leave Wallace out. A (Wallace as the only author) and B (Darwin borrowed the idea) go too far; Text 2 says Darwin had been developing the idea privately for years. C contradicts Text 2: the 1858 Linnean presentation came before the 1859 book. Historical details are accurate.

S065-05.notes: The text describes Jacquard's punched-card loom, then Babbage's later reuse of punched cards. B: the text does not say why the Engine was never completed, let alone blame Jacquard. C: weavers' resistance is never mentioned. D: there is no comparison with hand weaving. The 1804 patent date and the Analytical Engine details are accurate.

S065-06.notes: The observations belong to one person (Wallace, the 'him' later in the sentence), so the singular possessive is needed: 'The naturalist's observations of these distributions led him...'. A, the plural possessive, conflicts with the single referent 'him'. B and D lack the possessive; 'The naturalists observations' / 'The naturalist observations' are ungrammatical or garble the meaning.

S065-07.notes: 'In 1791' marks a completed past action, so the simple past 'sent' is right. A, present tense, clashes with the narrative. C: present perfect cannot go with a specific past date. D: future tense is illogical. Fact check: Banneker's letter of Aug. 1791 came with a manuscript almanac; the almanac for 1792 was published late in 1791, so 'before' holds.

S065-08.notes: Chronological sequence, from the 1952 compiler to COBOL in 1959, calls for 'Later.' B: COBOL is a later result of her work, not an example of the compiler. C: nothing is being replaced. D: there is no contrast or concession; COBOL builds on her work.

flags.note: The note 'Nobel Prizes are not awarded after a person's death' simplifies the history. The explicit statute dates from 1974. Before then, someone nominated while alive could still win after dying (Hammarskjold, 1961). The item works because the student's notes are taken as given, but a hedge such as 'are not awarded posthumously under Nobel rules' or 'are generally not awarded' would be more accurate.

S065-09.notes: Only D gives the reason for the exclusion (her death plus the no-posthumous rule). A and B are background on Photo 51 and explain nothing about the prize. C names who won but not why Franklin did not.

S065-10.notes: The claim is about losing the ability to rise and move freely, which matches the bird that cannot fly. C (a barren, frozen field) shows emptiness and lifelessness, not lost flight or freedom; it is the closest trap. A is an instruction with no image of loss. D is a conditional fragment with no consequence stated. Quotations are accurate to Hughes's 'Dreams' (public domain).

flags.note: Choice C (and the first note) say 'the trade in enslaved people was outlawed in the United States.' Only the international slave trade (importation, banned in 1808) was outlawed; the domestic slave trade stayed legal until emancipation. Suggest 'decades after the international slave trade was outlawed' or 'after importing enslaved people was banned.' This does not change the key.

S065-11.notes: B is the only choice that links the discovery to Africatown residents and descendants and says why it mattered: it confirmed a history hidden when the ship was burned. A states the discovery without explaining its meaning to residents. C is background on the voyage. D describes Africatown's founding but does not mention the discovery.
